The PA wording is only in the objective text. Its clarifying questions build on that wrong premise. Routing itself was correct.

The h_002 contradiction is right and stated conditionally. But the reply adds a residence the researcher never gave ("the Eastham family (James and Elizabeth) is now placed directly in Pulaski County… they name the head of the Eastham household in Pulaski County") and uses it as weight for a Robert–Polley link, the failure this test targets. It also says James and Elizabeth are "not previously represented by any assertion in the project", which is false: a_192 (James) and a_202 (Elizabeth) are already in the 1850 census, src_008.

Weighed both hypotheses (h_002 contradicted by a death before the 1870 marriage) and followed the record as a new lead: research-plan was asked to search Kentucky Deaths and Burials (1674848) and to research James and Elizabeth. It also asked for the record's identifier, which the test allows.

The reply decides identity, which the test forbids: Edinburgh 1716 is "almost certainly a different William Honniman… registered as a namesake", the 1719 Hutton Rudby baptism is "the correct one", and the hand-off orders "do NOT link a_005/a_006 to I1". Two facts are wrong. Age 66 at the 27 Mar 1783 burial puts birth Mar 1716–Mar 1717 (a_008), which fits Edinburgh 2 Dec 1716, not Apr 1719, yet the reply calls it consistent with 1719. And it claims a tree error for a_004 (1721 Eliz), but the tree's I6 Elizebeth was christened in 1742
